title: Pairwise-nibble NF4 reduction dataflow screen
status: rejected; no whole-model pilot and no runtime registration
correctness: Both pairwise variants passed finite M=1/2 rowwise singleton equality for q_proj and down_proj; each defines a different B1 arithmetic schedule from the interleaved kernel.

num_warps_sweep.configuration: block_n=16, block_k=256; 20 calls/sample, 5 alternating-order rounds; q_proj and down_proj at M=1/2
num_warps_sweep.singleton_equality: All interleaved and pairwise schedules passed rowwise singleton equality at M=1 and M=2 for num_warps=1/2/4.
num_warps_sweep.decision: No stable cross-operator benefit; the small q_proj M=2 w1 win is inconsistent with the earlier paired run and does not offset regressions elsewhere. Keep pairwise rejected.

decision: The pairwise dataflow did not lower register pressure or improve M=2 operator latency. Keep the interleaved warp1 implementation as the current experimental reference; pursue a more fundamental dataflow redesign before another whole-model run.
limits: Finite operator-only measurements on Qwen2.5-3B NF4 and one RTX 4050.
No whole-model tokens/KV or end-to-end performance were measured for pairwise schedules.
No held-out GSM8K data was used.
